prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending just below the hip line. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips just below her hip line, where her thighs have barely begun to separate, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman in Hong Kong-style makeup — fair matte skin with a soft powdery finish, thin sharply arched brows, soft brown and rose eyeshadow, a fine black liner with a small flick, long curled lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a strong rose-red blush on the apples of the cheeks, deep glossy red lips with a defined edge, hair set in glossy voluminous old-film waves, a poised, glamorous expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a large vintage pearl clip earring.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, both thighs just beginning to separate.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest, belly, hips and the very tops of both thighs — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of banded black and white onyx, deep glossy black layered with crisp pale cream bands running horizontally through it, polished to a hard mirror sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone. Just below her hip line, where the two thighs have only just begun to separate, each one individually curves inward and rounds off into its own small, smooth, polished tip — the two tips stay clearly distinct even this close together, never merging into one single base — the stone simply reaching its natural end at the top of each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque banded onyx — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same cool, hard, dense solidity throughout, catching light only as bright highlights on its polished surface, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the stone.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the stone's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip at the end of each thigh stub is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep glossy black on one side and a warm cream on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so black light glances off the left half and cream light glances off the right half, catching in bright reflections. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
